properties.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 445 AM EST.

* At 217 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Camp Holly Fish Camp, West Melbourne, Suntree,
Viera, Melbourne Village, June Park.

properties.description:

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:04AM MST until November 3 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Woodruff to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At midnight MST, river gauges along the Little Colorado River
have reported significant rises this evening. The guage at the
Winslow has exceeded Minor Flood stage. Further rises are
expected to occur through the overnight from upstream heavy
rainfall. Flooding is already ongoing.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Joseph City:
At 10:30pm MST the stage was 5.67 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.51 feet is expected at 12:00pm MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.
At 9.0 feet: Flood stage. Minor overflow on right (north) bank,
with no threat to any buildings, mainly rural countryside.

For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 11:00pm MST the stage was 19.54 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 29.04 feet is expected at 6:00am MST
Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
At 19.0 feet: Overflow on right bank. Water approaches Ames Acres
and Bushman Acres on left bank in Winslow area. Erosion is likely
on the levee on the left bank. Downstream, with approximately 18
hour lag time, the approaches to the bridge over the river on
Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood and evacuations of
homes near the intersection of Navajo Route 2 and Navajo Route 71
are conducted.
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.

For Little Colorado at Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 10:30pm MST the stage was 6.54 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 21.64 feet is expected at 11:00am MST
Monday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.
At 25.0 feet: Levee overtopped. Major flooding.

For Little Colorado River at Little Colorado River Near Woodruff:
At 10:30pm MST the stage was 11.67 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 25.29 feet is expected at 7:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Bankfull. Portions of residential yards flooded.
At 26.0 feet: River reaches pedestrian bridge and top of river
gage apparatus. Accurate river gage readings unlikely above this
point.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Holbrook, Joseph City, Leupp, Birdsprings, Woodruff,
Manila, Hibbard, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State
Park, Rosedale Heights, Clearview Heights, Jackrabbit and Clear
Creek Reservoir.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground and Hunt Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday.

isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even

properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 2 at 1:06AM EST until November 4 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
An upper level low will will continue to influence storms in the
Gulf and Bahamas through Monday. With the lack of a strong synoptic
surface forcing mechanism, predictability as to where and when heavy
rain will fall remains low. However, the environment continues to
support the potential for heavy rainfall and slow moving cells.

* WHAT...Heavy rain may cause, or worsen ongoing urban and street
flooding.

* WHERE...All of South Florida

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered areas of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and those areas, and others, have the
potential to be impacted again on Monday. Forecast amounts look
very similar to yesterday, with common amounts of 1 to 3 inches
where showers and storms occur. Scattered locations around south
Florida may see closer to 3 to 5 inches of rain. The more
isolated high end amounts have the potential to peak around 6 to
9 inches. These amounts could accumulate rather quickly, on the
order of 2 to 4 hours.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 9 feet in the surf zone
and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM ChST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated, long-period, north-northwest
swell from Typhoon In-fa will continue to produce hazardous
surf and a high risk of rip currents along north facing reefs
through tonight, likely diminishing below hazardous levels by
late tonight as swells steadily diminish. Hazardous surf of 7 to
9 feet early tonight is expected to diminish below hazardous
levels, becoming 6 to 8 feet by late tonight.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life
threatening. Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the
water due to dangerous surf conditions. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

through the remainder of this evening from earlier heavy
rainfall. Emergency management has reported evacuations along the

-   - For the Verde River at Clarkdale:

flood along the Verde River downstream in Camp Verde to Beasley

dangers of flooding.

attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

can be impacted between 7 and 7.7 feet. Water will be on Highway 4
at mile marker 1, 2 and 13.  Homes near the river in San Ysidro
could be impacted.

expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Graham County in southeastern Arizona...
Greenlee County in southeastern Arizona...

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

heavy rain had fallen over portions of eastern Graham and

heavy flows. Flooding of small streams is ongoing.

Airport, Roper Lake State Park, Hannagan Meadow, Blue, Duncan,

SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SUNDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...San Juan Mountains
*WHEN... From 4:30 PM Sunday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS... Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous
avalanches large enough to bury a human.
*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS... A potent winter storm increases
avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.


Beyer

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:06PM MST until November 2 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River Near Archuleta affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...San Juan River near Archuleta.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor flooding is possible with inundation
to structures located close to the river from near Archuleta to
Bloomfield.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 PM MST Sunday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 PM MST Sunday was 7.1 feet. Due to high uncertainty, the
crest forecast will likely change in future updates.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 3.8 feet Sunday,
November 08.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.2
feet on 03/27/1955.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please heed any evacuation orders from local authorities.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 215 AM MST.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:58PM MST until November 2 at 1:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Moenkopi Wash in Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 100 AM MST Monday.

* At 458 PM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise above
action stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin. Further
rises are expected, with water levels expected to exceed major
flood stage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 4:45pm MST the stage was 26.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 29.45 feet is expected at 5:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 3:56PM PST until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:37PM MST until November 2 at 4:30PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the South Fork Rio Grande and mainstem Rio
Grande through South Fork caused by rain and snowmelt is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County in south central Colorado...
West Central Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the South Fork Rio Grande and mainstem Rio
Grande through South Fork is expected. Additional flooding of
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Numerous roads remain closed due to
flooding. Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
rainfall and upstream snowmelt.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 433 PM MST, Rain and snowmelt is occurring, and will cause
flooding. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen on top of
melting snow. Stream gauge data indicates that the South Fork Rio
Grande at South Fork will be reaching flood stage soon.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Fork and areas along Highway 160 up to Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 2:09PM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected today into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely and some rivers may
flood. If river flooding materializes, it will likely continue
into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 10:29AM PST until November 2 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Minor tidal overflow during high tides.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Minor flood impacts are possible during high tides
with water flowing over normally dry sand and to lower parking
lots or paths. Moderate beach erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional flood impacts are likely into
next weekend with tides reaching 7 ft as early as Friday. Tides
will peak over the weekend into early next week 7.0-7.8 ft.
Elevated surf may increase flood impacts during this time,
especially across west to northwest facing beaches. Reminder,
tides mentioned have been corrected to reflect the most recent
trends in actual tide observations.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

reflect the current trends in actual tide observations.

properties.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 10:37PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST Sunday through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...West Elk Mountains, Elk Mountains, San Juan Mountains, and
La Plata Mountains
*WHEN...From 4:30 PM Saturday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS...Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous
avalanches large enough to bury a human.

*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...A potent winter storm increases
avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett

...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

La Plata River at Hesperus affecting La Plata County.

For the La Plata River...including Hesperus...Minor flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 900 AM MST.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...La Plata River at Hesperus.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM MDT Saturday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Sunday
evening to a crest of 5.8 feet late Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.8
feet on 05/21/2005.
